title: Determining individual radiation sensitivity for risk assessment in radiation therapy.
summary: Patients with cancer who undergo radiation therapy are at low risk of experiencing adverse effects from the treatment. However, certain groups of patients repeatedly experience these effects. These include patients with genetic disorders or autoimmune diseases, and those receiving certain medications. Our first objective is to identify diseases associated with increased radiation sensitivity and determine the cause of this sensitivity. Secondly, we want to study whether clinical characteristics can be used to predict radiation sensitivity.
conditions: Patients with breast cancer risk genes, rare genetic disorders, lupus erythematosus, vitiligo, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, patients taking kinase inhibitors

interventions.name: Patient groups suspected of having genetic or autoimmune diseases that could cause increased sensitivity to radiation are studied for these conditions.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with genetic variants suspected of inducing increased radiation sensitivity.
Patients with autoimmune diseases suspected of inducing increased radiation sensitivity.
Patients with tumors and taking kinase inhibitors.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients < 18 years of age, with the exception of:
Genetic background of the germ line in childhood tumors.
Children with Fanconi anemia.
